sections.heading: Yangon: Myanmar's Largest City and Former Capital
paragraphs: Yangon (formerly Rangoon) is Myanmar's largest city, founded in its present form in the mid-1750s by King Alaungpaya as a port. [2] It handles more than four-fifths of the country's foreign commerce. The British occupied it during two Anglo-Burmese Wars in the 19th century, and after full British annexation in 1886, it became the colonial capital. In 2005, Myanmar's government began relocating offices to Naypyidaw, about 200 miles north -- Yangon remains the country's commercial and largest city even though it's no longer the seat of government.
